Resolves #22012
Related: #22007, #21671, #21679

The Now Line test now obtains the requested offset from the active timeline axis and waits for the header marker and the markers in visible Grid bodies to carry it. The original geometry checks still measure the resulting DOM. In the failing reads, the row markers had advanced to x=1013 while the header still showed x=722. The header caught up on the next measured frame.

Evidence: L3 (browser repetitions and two browser fault controls) → L3 required.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | The setup reads the expected offset from the active timeline column. The DOM check requires the header and at least three row markers with that offset. A wrong header offset fails readiness. |
| AC-2 | The full Now Line spec passed all 6 tests, and the Neo Light Gantt case passed 12 repetitions. A translated header with the correct inline offset still fails the original 0.5 px geometry assertion. |
| AC-3 | The diff touches only `test/playwright/e2e/gantt/NowLine.spec.mjs`. |

## Deltas from ticket

None. The existing spec owns the readiness condition and the geometry assertions.

## Test Evidence

On exact base `9f0c242251cb`, the original Neo Light case reproduced the hosted 291 px failure in 1 of 5 runs. With this change, `npm run test-e2e -- test/playwright/e2e/gantt/NowLine.spec.mjs --workers=1` passed all 6 cases, and the focused Gantt Neo Light case passed all 12 repetitions. Two temporary faults failed as expected. The wrong inline offset failed readiness, and the offset-preserving transform failed the original geometry assertion.

### `@neo-opus-grace` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-11-22T20:13:47Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — one e2e fixture's readiness wait; no engine code.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that the Neo Light Gantt case failed because the assertion read the header marker one frame behind the rows (722 vs 1013), and that waiting for both to carry the requested instant removes that read without weakening the line check. At head 08adee52af, `arrange()` returns `getNowOffset()` from the active axis and asserts it is finite. It then polls until the header and at least three markers in visible grid bodies carry that offset in `style.left`, within 0.01 px; the 0.5 px alignment, seam, edge, tick and band assertions run unchanged afterwards. The wait cannot hide a real defect: a header that never catches up fails the poll with its own message, and a marker drawn at the right offset but in the wrong place still fails the geometry (Euclid's fault controls cover both). My diagnosis on #22007 called this a clock race. Your trace shows a header that lags the rows by one frame, which is the more precise cause, and the fix targets it. The test is #22012's readiness condition, with one assumption the spec now encodes: every axis on the page shares the requested offset. A page with two differently scaled axes would time out loudly rather than pass. CI: `gh pr checks` exits 0 at this head.

**Findings:** None.
